summary: Pipeline order is normative: includes inline before parsing (a .md page converts first, then inlines — §10.1); layouts before URL phases; §11.1→§11.2→§11.3; collisions before write; reference check on temp tree; publish last
Best-effort composition: a problem in one page never stops analysis of others; all problems in the site reported in one pass
Preservation: all bytes outside an edited span are preserved exactly; the layout's text is the base document
Include splice: the include element or SSI comment is replaced by the included file's processed contents
Slot fill: the slot element is replaced by the fill elements in page order; the consumed slot attribute is removed; nothing else about a fill's markup changes
Slot fallback: slot start/end tags removed, inner bytes kept as written
Children replacement: the element's children are replaced by the default content; the element itself, tag and attributes, stays
Unwrap: page's first <main> start tag and matching end tag deleted; inner bytes stay in place
Removal: removed elements are removed entirely; removed attributes (data-layout, consumed slot) are removed cleanly; removal changes nothing else
Head replacement in place: the page's element(s) take the layout element's position in page order; other same-key layout elements removed per S07
Head append: appended head elements land at the end of the layout's head content, in page-source order
Title join: layout title inner text becomes pageText + " " + layoutText, both trimmed; layout's title tag kept
Root attributes: class = layout tokens then page tokens not already present; overridden attr edited in place; new attr inserted before closing > in page order
Default content: nodes kept in source order with interior text preserved as written; boundary whitespace-only text nodes are not significant
Output shell (doctype, html, head, body tags) is the layout's; page's doctype/shell not emitted; page with no layout emitted from its own text (layout-less .md: converted body inside the §10.7 shell)
--exclude repeatable; unify.yaml key exclude is a list; default is the single glob _*; user globs replace the default
Pattern without / tested against every path segment of the source-root-relative path
Pattern with / tested against the full source-root-relative path with * ** ? […] semantics
A matched directory segment excludes the entire subtree; files inside a _-directory need no own underscore
Excluded files are never emitted but remain build material: includable and usable as layouts
Underscore guard: an emitted _-prefixed page or a path containing a _-prefixed directory segment is a problem naming the file and the fixing --exclude line
The guard does not cover _-prefixed non-page files; the exclude-replacement recipe ships _headers/_redirects cleanly
Never-shipped list exactly: output dir inside root, .git/.hg/.svn, node_modules, .env and .env.*, unify.yaml; not replaceable; never scanned; dotfiles ship
Mirror copy: every emitted asset copied byte-for-byte to the same source-root-relative path
Symlinks followed only while resolving inside the source root; outside → treated as absent with advisory A12

Defaulted-source notice: when the source root defaulted to the working directory (no --source flag, no unify.yaml source key, no src/), the stdout summary reports the copied-file count and points at --dry-run; explicit --source (even .) or an existing src/ suppresses it; never a diagnostic, never affects exit

Fragments: a name ending .fragment.html is not a page - mirror-copied byte-for-byte, never composed or rewritten, never moved by --pretty-urls, insides not reference-checked (runtime resolution base is the consuming page), still an ordinary include target; references to it are checked and rewritten normally; underscore still excludes it
SSI virtual="P" resolves against the source root; leading / permitted and equivalent
SSI file="P" must be relative and resolves against dirname of the including file
<include src="P">: leading / resolves from source root, else relative to the including file
Resolved include path escaping the source root is a problem (not-found shape); traversal safety internal and always on
Include target must exist and end .html/.md; otherwise a located problem with fix lines including spelling-and-casing
A .md include target is converted first (frontmatter stripped and ignored, heading ids applied); .html used verbatim
Include targets' own includes process recursively before splicing
Include cycle detection by resolved-path stack; depth cap 10 inclusive (a chain ten deep builds, the include pushing an eleventh is the problem); both problems print the full chain
<include> without src is a problem
<include> with non-whitespace content between its tags is a problem; includes never take fills
Void <include> builds identically and carries advisory A01

Inlining is textual and pre-parse for HTML hosts (in Markdown: post-conversion, §10.1 — timing is the only difference): includes work anywhere (head, Markdown); fragment top-level elements become the host's (may carry slot= fills or contribute <slot> elements)
Layout selection order, first match wins: data-layout=none / frontmatter layout:none; data-layout=V; frontmatter layout:V; nearest _layout.html walking up; else none
Discovery walk is by file name; the layout file's excluded status is irrelevant
Explicit layout value not ending .html (bare name) is a problem before any existence check
Layout path resolution: / from source root, else relative to the declaring file
Layout target missing or escaping the source root is a problem with the include-not-found shape including the casing fix line
data-layout on a non-root element is a problem naming <include src> as the replacement
Any data-unify attribute anywhere in any source file — excluded files included; only the never-shipped list escapes scanning — is a problem naming the v0.7.0 spelling
Any class token beginning unify- anywhere in any source file (excluded files included) is a problem naming the slot spelling
data-layout never appears in output (removed per S07, including the none form)
A <script> carrying data-polyfill is removed entirely from built output
A layout that itself declares data-layout (any value, including none) is a problem P15 - layout chaining is not supported in v0.7.0; never a silent no-op
Sinks are the <slot> elements in the layout's <body> (skipping any inside <template>) plus the layout's first <main>; neither → sink-less
First bare <slot> is the default slot; further bare slots get advisory A13 (duplicated construct) and render their fallback
First <slot name=X> per X receives X's fills; a repeated name gets advisory A13 and later ones render their fallback
A <slot> outside a layout's <body> (in any page, or a layout's <head>) is problem P20 and is replaced by its own children
Duplicate <main> in a layout: the first wins, advisory A13

When the layout has at least one sink, the page's first <main> — in document order, at any depth, not only top level — is unwrapped once (S06); a <main> inside the first survives; no other element is unwrapped

Fills are the direct element children of the page body and of the page's first <main> wherever it sat, carrying a non-empty slot attribute; slot="" counts as absent; slot anywhere else is never touched or reported
Default content is everything else in the page body - elements, text, comments - in source order (S12)
For each name with fills, <slot name> is replaced by the fills in page order (S03)
A fill naming a slot the layout lacks: advisory A02, slot attribute consumed, element stays in place in the default-content sequence
Each unfilled named slot is replaced by its own children (S04); fallback content is plain markup (a nested slot is P16/MRG-19); slots inside <template> ship as written
Default slot present → default content replaces it; empty default content → the default slot renders its fallback
No default slot, layout has <main> → default content replaces <main>'s children (S05); empty default content → <main> keeps its children
No default slot, no <main>, named slots exist, default content non-empty → problem (content would vanish)
Every message about a slot or a layout names the layout file it was checked against
Sink-less layout: whole <body> is the default slot; page body children replace layout body children verbatim (S05, no unwrap); head-only layout is legitimate
A <header>/<footer> that is not a fill is default content: it ships in place and is not reported (A03 retired)

The content-loss law: authored content is never dropped without failing the build; every rule places content or raises a problem (enforced across all fixtures via diagnosticsExhaustive + tree assertions)
Slots do not nest: a <slot> inside another slot's fallback content is a problem P16 - fallback content is plain markup

The merge requires a <body> on both sides: a missing one is P21 at the file that lacks it and the page is not built; an empty resolved layout file is this problem, never a silent no-layout; a body-less layout never publishes its own text as the page
Charset: page's dropped in favor of layout's which stays first; layout without one -> page's kept and moved first; identical silent; different -> advisory A08
Title joined per S10 in the layout title's position; empty/whitespace page title counts as absent; layout without <title> → page's title appends with its own text

Meta name/property keyed ASCII case-insensitively: replaces in place (S08); multiple page elements with one key all kept; dedup only crosses the layout/page boundary; no layout counterpart → appends (fixture M1); http-equiv not keyed → appends
link rel=canonical replaces in place; one canonical, never two
link with icon in its rel token list (covers shortcut icon, ASCII case-insensitive): all layout icon links removed, page set takes the first one's position; apple-touch-icon not keyed
Stylesheet/script-src dedup by URL compared after §11.1 resolution — page copy dropped, layout position stands; inline script/style with byte-identical content: page copy dropped
Everything else appends after the layout's head content in page-source order (S09); page CSS loads last
On html/body only: page class tokens appended to the layout's without repeats
Any other attribute the page sets wins: edited in place if the layout had it, inserted before > otherwise
data-layout and consumed slot attributes are removed before the root-attribute merge; a page cannot remove a layout attribute; attributes merge nowhere else
CommonMark, no extensions beyond §10.4 heading ids; output filename swaps .md for .html

Include timing in Markdown: conversion first — include tags/SSI comments pass through the converter as raw HTML and resolve on the converted output; fragment contents are spliced verbatim, never converted; a .md include target converts exactly once
Layout rules apply exactly as for an HTML page whose body is the converted output and whose head is synthesized from frontmatter
Frontmatter is YAML between --- fences at the very start of the file
title key becomes the page's <title>, then merges per §8 row 2
layout key drives layout selection per §6.1
class key adds class tokens to the page's <body>
lang and dir keys set those attributes on <html>
Any other scalar key becomes <meta name="KEY" content="VALUE">
og: block entries become <meta property="og:K" content="V">
Any other block (twitter: …) entries become <meta name="BLOCK:K" content="V">
A list value emits one <meta> per item, in order
Synthesized elements merge per §8 as if page-written; serialization fixed: double-quoted attributes, name/property before content, <title>TEXT</title>
No other reserved keys: date/tags/categories/draft/permalink/slug become plain metas; draft:true publishes; a leading underscore holds a page back
No frontmatter title → text of the first <h1> in the converted body with inline markup stripped; neither → no page title, the layout's stands alone
Heading id algorithm: lowercase, whitespace runs to single hyphens, drop non-letter/digit/hyphen (Unicode kept), trim hyphens, -2/-3 on repeats; explicit id kept; HTML pages never touched
Frontmatter fence at byte 0 of an .html page is a problem
A literal <head> element in a Markdown body is a problem

The include-block extension: a line beginning <include starts an HTML block (as if include were on CommonMark's type-6 list); line-initial include/SSI splices as a block, in-paragraph include splices inline; include syntax in a code fence or code span is escaped text, never a directive

Layout-less .md emits inside the minimal synthesized shell: doctype; <html> with frontmatter lang/dir; <head> with charset first, then title when one exists, then metas in source order; <body> with frontmatter class holding the converted body; nothing else synthesized

Value serialization: plain scalars as source text (true, 2026-01-01, 0.50 as written — no YAML coercion); quoted scalars unquoted; block scalars as YAML defines; empty value → empty string; lists compose with blocks (one meta per item)

Provenance rewriting applies to every URL in href, src, srcset (each URL, descriptors untouched), poster, and the content of the URL-valued og:/twitter: metas §12 names — one list, so a layout's relative og:image is re-rooted like the beside it, rather than emitting a URL that resolves against each page and then failing §12 — after includes and layouts, before §11.2/§11.3; the URL part of a meta http-equiv=refresh content is on the same list and is URL-13
Skipped: scheme or // prefix, mailto/tel/data/javascript, fragment-only, empty values
Never reached: url() inside <style> blocks or style attributes — write those root-relative or in stylesheet files
A URL starting with / is unchanged by §11.1
A relative URL whose provenance is a layout or include file resolves against that file's directory and is emitted root-relative
A relative URL whose provenance is the page stays exactly as written — unless the page's output moved (--pretty-urls), then resolved and emitted root-relative
Pretty files: every page output X.html moves to X/index.html except any index.html and the root 404.html
Pretty links: after §11.1, every internal URL resolving to an emitted page's .html output is rewritten resolve-first then transformed, emitted root-relative (the eight-row table)
Pretty preserves untouched: external URLs, mailto/tel/data, fragment-only, URLs to non-page files; query and fragment always survive

base-url is the whole address (scheme+domain); a bare path is a usage error, exit 2. Its path part prefixes every root-relative URL in href/src/srcset/poster plus root-relative og:/twitter: meta content; root-relative means ONE leading slash, so a protocol-relative //host/path is absolute and is left exactly as written, like every other absolute form §11.1 skips

base-url origin is prepended to og:/twitter: content and canonical href — absolutization is always origin + path prefix (og:image /assets/x.jpg under https://host/repo/ emits https://host/repo/assets/x.jpg)
base-url leaves non-root-relative values untouched; source files stay rooted at /; order §11.1→§11.2→§11.3

Check scope: every emitted HTML file's href/src/srcset/poster, link href for every rel, and the content of the URL-VALUED og:/twitter: metas (og:url/image/audio/video, twitter:image/player and their :url/:secure_url/:src/:stream forms) in EVERY spelling — relative, root-relative, or absolute, because a test on the value checked two spellings and silently skipped the third; plus url() in every emitted CSS file, <style> block, and style attribute; two further sources are checked and have their own rules — the meta refresh URL (REF-09) and root-relative string values inside JSON-LD (REF-10)

Internal = after stripping the base-url prefix (path prefix, or the full origin+path base when a full URL was given — absolutized values stay checkable), root-relative or relative (resolved against the containing output file's URL); query/fragment stripped; external and mailto/tel/data/fragment-only skipped
A directory URL (trailing / or empty path) checks for index.html within it
A URL resolving to no emitted file is a problem naming the source file, the reference, and the line where known
Case is compared byte-for-byte; a reference matching only case-insensitively fails
#fragment targets are not validated against ids

A reference resolving to the output path of a source page that exists but failed to compose is NOT reported (its own problem already blocks the publish); a target with no source file, and an excluded-but-existing target, still fail
Two sources producing one output path is a problem naming both sources
A --pretty-urls move landing on another source's output is a problem naming both sources

Two outputs differing only by letter case: advisory A11, quoting the located path once — a source pair colliding on that same output path (P12) must not put it on both sides of the sentence. The group is one case-folded form but the sentence names one representative per NFC form, escaped, and is not printed when that leaves nothing to name: a pair `toLowerCase` merges only because it collapsed a canonical singleton (U+212A KELVIN SIGN and kin) differs by no case at all and is A16's
Pages and assets cannot collide by construction; collisions detected before any write; no last-write-wins anywhere

Two outputs that one host folding sees as one name, where the folding is not case alone, are advisory A16; the key is NFC and THEN case-folded because the common normalizing host folds both at once, so the group CONTAINS A11's whenever a name appears in both a second case and a second form. The guarantee is that each advisory says only what is true of what it names — A11 names ONLY pairs differing by case (its group is one case fold, its representatives one per NFC form, so any two it names differ in NFC) and A16 makes no per-pair claim at all, asserting only the folding that merges its whole group, because a group can hold a pure-ASCII case pair (Kilo.html/kilo.html beside U+212A Kilo.html) about which no form claim is true. Not a partition: a group that is A11's entirely — every member the same after case folding AND every member a distinct NFC form — is skipped, both halves load-bearing (case-fold alone hands the KELVIN pair to A11, form alone makes the macOS pair silent in both), and every surviving group is quoted in full, one escaped spelling per member, so a name colliding in both ways is named by both. The table is closed because §20.5's address function is injective over output paths (encodeURIComponent escapes % so decoding inverts it, and about/index.html is the only path yielding /about/), leaving only the host's own name foldings
Two severities only: problem and advisory; never "warning", "error:", or rule codes
Exit 0: published (with --dry-run: would have)
Exit 1: problems found (or advisories under --strict); nothing published; previous output untouched
Exit 2: invalid usage or fatal environment error (unknown flag, missing source dir, --clean containment refusal, port in use)
Diagnostics to stderr; build summary and --dry-run list to stdout; both ordered by path then line; two runs print the same bytes
Every diagnostic line begins FILE:LINE: SEVERITY: (line omitted when unknown); prefix and severity token are stable contract, message prose is not
Continuation lines indented two spaces: in: and fix:; path-shaped messages always include the spelling-and-casing fix line
Cycle and depth messages print the full chain joined with " → "
DEBUG=1 adds stack traces
Advisory discipline: unify init && unify build --dry-run --strict exits 0; an advisory firing on a correct site is a bug in the advisory

Attribution conventions are contract: cycle/depth problems locate at the outermost include site; collision problems at the path-ordered first colliding source; every other located diagnostic — §6 layout selection, §7 composition, §8 charset advisory, §12 references — at the provenance file of the offending markup and its line IN that file, never the host post-inlining line

A line that cannot be mapped to the named file is omitted, not guessed: the FILE: SEVERITY: form is used (a .md page converts before inlining, so an offset attributed to Markdown source indexes converted HTML)

Diagnostics are deduplicated before counting or printing: same file, line, severity, message, in: and fix: lines = one diagnostic; genuinely distinct faults that print identically (a relative url() in shared chrome resolving per consumer) are distinguished by resolved target and both printed
Problem: include target missing, wrong extension, or escaping the source root
Problem: include cycle or depth over 10, chain printed
Problem: <include> without src; <include> with non-whitespace content
Problem: layout reference not a .html path (bare name)
Problem: layout target missing or escaping the source root
Problem: data-layout on a non-root element
Problem: data-unify attribute; unify- class token
Problem: unaddressed page content with no sink in a slotted layout
Problem: frontmatter in an .html page
Problem: literal <head> in a Markdown body
Problem: output collision
Problem: broken internal reference
Problem: emitted _-prefixed page or _-directory path
Problem: a layout declares data-layout - layout chaining is not supported in v0.7.0
Problem: a <slot> nested inside another slot's fallback content - slots do not nest
Problem: a frontmatter value with no text form - a mapping nested below a key that already names one, or a list item that is itself a mapping or list
Problem: frontmatter is not valid YAML - a parse failure, distinct from P17's shape rule
Problem: a named slot inside the layout's default-content sink main, with no bare slot - the two rules target overlapping spans
Problem: <slot> outside a layout's <body> (anywhere in a page, or in a layout's <head>); the fix names the spelling that belongs in that file. Was advisory A04
Problem: a page or layout with no <body> element where a merge requires one; attributed file-level to the file that lacks it, fix spelled for that file's kind
Advisory: void <include> used
Advisory: fill names a slot the layout doesn't have; content stayed in the page flow
Advisory: page charset differs from the layout's, layout's kept
Advisory: working-format file emitted; closed extension list .psd .ai .sketch .fig .xcf
Advisory: a file used as a layout or include also ships as its own page

Advisory: output paths differing only by case; the located path opens the sentence and is not repeated in the list that follows; each path is escaped, one representative per NFC form is named, and the advisory is not printed when that leaves nothing to name — so a pair that is one name in two forms never draws this sentence

Advisory: output paths a host folding normalization form AND letter case together sees as one file, the message saying exactly that and asserting no form relationship between any two members since the group may hold a pure-ASCII case pair; ranges over output paths so a pair of assets counts exactly as a pair of pages does; each path is quoted with its non-ASCII code points escaped because the two print identically and an advisory quoting one string twice names no edit the author can make; EVERY distinct spelling in the group is named, since all of them are one file on a normalizing host and a sentence omitting one describes a rename that does not resolve the collision; the FILE locator stays the real path, the located path is quoted once and never repeated in the list that follows, and the files still ship
Advisory: symlink resolving outside the source root, treated as absent
Advisory: duplicated construct of which only the first counts - second bare <slot>, repeated slot name, or second <main>; message names the construct

Advisory: known deployment file at the source root held back by the exclude set (maintained list, non-normative; today _headers, _redirects, _routes.json, _worker.js); names the file and the --exclude line that ships it; source-root names only
Transactional publish: zero problems → publish; any problem → previous output byte-for-byte untouched and exit 1
Publish sync: unchanged files not rewritten; files no longer produced deleted; new/changed land via temp-then-rename
--clean empties the output directory first; refuses with exit 2 when the output directory is, or contains, the source root or the working directory - not when it merely sits inside them
--dry-run runs the entire pipeline through the report with no writes at all
Saves coalesce into one rebuild; a save landing mid-rebuild queues exactly one follow-up; no change dropped
Every rebuild is full; watch output after any edit sequence is identical to a fresh unify build
Watch writes are minimal and atomic: unchanged files untouched, temp-then-rename, precise deletions; --clean applies only at startup
While watching, a failing page is emitted as a default error page carrying the located diagnostics, replaced on next success; unify build never emits error pages
unify dev = watch + static server on localhost:port (default 3000) serving the output directory with directory indexes and a 404 page, plus a reload event stream
The reload script is injected only into HTML responses dev serves and never exists in the output directory
No proxying, HTTPS, middleware, or config in dev — permanently (asserted by the closed CLI surface test: unknown flags exit 2)
--dry-run report: stdout, one list ordered by output path, one line per action, verbs write/copy/delete only
Every write line names its inputs: the source page and the layout it resolved to
Under --dry-run, diagnostics print to stderr exactly as a real build would
--dry-run states the address it is building for (base-url, or the domain root when unset), and each write/copy row carries the URL that file answers to
unify.yaml keys are the long option names: source output clean exclude pretty-urls base-url strict port; exclude replaces the default like the flag
CLI flags win over unify.yaml on conflict
No behavior exists that only the file can express; the file itself is never emitted

Every template scaffolds into src/ beside a dist-free root and exercises each primitive exactly once: one include (nav), automatic _layout.html, one named slot with fallback (footer) plus a page filling it, one data-layout=none page (404.html), and _includes/
Scaffolded layout declares <meta charset="utf-8">; a plain HTML comment above each slot; starter stylesheet includes slot { display: contents }; built pages contain no <slot> elements

The blog template ships _scripts/gen.mjs (zero dependencies, opening comment naming the authoring rules' literal node _scripts/gen.mjs && unify build) reading posts/*.md and _data/authors.json and writing blog.html and feed.xml into the source tree, shipped pre-generated: rerunning the script reproduces the checked-in tree byte-for-byte
unify init && unify build --dry-run --strict exits 0 (asserted per template)

The blog generator teaches field privacy: _data/authors.json carries a private email beside public fields; gen.mjs names the fields it emits (never spreads the record), so the email appears in no generated file and nowhere in built output; both generated files carry the "generated by _scripts/gen.mjs — edit the data, not this file" marker
Worked example: nested include with relative resolution, exact
Worked example C1: golden path, <main> default with unwrap, exact
Worked example C2: named slot replaces the element, exact body
Worked example C3: unfilled slot renders its fallback, exact body
Worked example C4: multiple fills one name, in page order
Worked example C5: fill to a nonexistent slot — advisory A02, content preserved
Worked example C6: bare slot inside <main>, pinning by markup
Worked example C8: sink-less head-only passthrough, exact
Worked example C9: slots inside <template> never touched
Worked example: the whole head-merge table at once, exact
Worked example: root-attribute merge one-liner
Worked example: Markdown end to end, exact
Worked example C7: a layout declaring data-layout is a problem P15 (realized as landmine layout-declares-layout)

Membership: one record per composed page, in output-path order; assets, .fragment.html files, excluded sources, and pages that failed to compose have no record; a page with no metadata still gets a complete record

Extraction reads the emitted text only (post-includes, post-Markdown, post-composition, post-§11); layout-supplied metadata is read per shipping page; <template> contents are never scanned; deriving the manifest changes no output, diagnostic, or exit code

Every record carries every field; absent scalars are null and absent lists are []; text content resolves numeric and HTML 4.01 named character references (leaving unknown ones as written), omits script/style/template/noscript subtrees, contributes one space on entering and leaving every non-inline element, collapses whitespace runs to one space, and trims; image width/height are read only when the url came from og:image

Single-valued fields keep the first accepted declaration in document order; differing repeats append one conflicts entry {field, kept, discarded} ordered by field name; identical repeats are not conflicts; a conflict is data, never a §14 diagnostic

path is publish.js's urlForOutputPath (index.html dropped, --base-url path prefix applied) with every output-path segment percent-encoded and the base-url prefix left alone; url is origin+path with --base-url and null without it

robots is parsed from EVERY <meta name="robots"> the page emits, not the first — a crawler reads the union, and splitting noindex, nofollow across two tags is a documented spelling of one policy; raw is every value comma-joined in document order, directives are that split lowercased, indexable is false on noindex/none and followable on nofollow/none; unknown directives are preserved and change nothing; a crawler-specific meta is never read and robots.txt is never read into a page record; robots is correspondingly absent from §20.4's conflict set
text is the text content of the first <main>, else <body>, else the whole document

jsonLd is one {raw, data, error} per ld+json script in document order, parsing never throws; schemaType is the first of <meta name="schema"> or a single-object string @type, and arrays/@graph/missing/non-string @type declare nothing

linksOut holds deduplicated sorted output paths of linked pages that have records, after base-url stripping, with query/fragment discarded and skipped-URL schemes excluded; linksIn is its exact reverse

Activation is --base-url and governs the whole section, §21.6 included: without it no sitemap is emitted, an authored one is an ordinary mirror-copied asset, and nothing about sitemaps is reported; generation is additive, appears in --dry-run, and participates in transactional publish

Membership is the closed list: has a record, robots.indexable, output path is not 404.html, and self-canonical (no canonical, or one resolving to its own output path via §12's resolution); entries appear in manifest order

Each entry is <loc> = record.url, percent-encoded by §20.5 and then XML-escaped, plus <lastmod> only when dateModified.iso is non-null; never the build clock, filesystem time, filename, Git history, or datePublished; no changefreq and no priority

urlset in the sitemaps 0.9 namespace, UTF-8, newline-terminated, byte-identical across runs; over 50,000 URLs or 50 MiB the output is a sitemap index at sitemap.xml naming sitemap-1.xml, sitemap-2.xml, filled in manifest order
An authored sitemap.xml suppresses generation entirely and ships byte-for-byte; a generated path occupied by an emitted source file is P22 located at that file, with generation suppressed

Every internal <loc> in an emitted output-root sitemap, generated or authored, must resolve to an emitted file or raise P13 located at the sitemap; other-origin values are skipped rather than fetched; the document is parsed, so a <loc> in a comment declares nothing, a CDATA-wrapped value is the value, and a namespace-prefixed loc is a loc
Generated discovery artifact's output path already occupied by a file emitted from source; located at the occupying source file; generation suppressed rather than overwriting

iso is the declared value only when it is well-formed W3C-DTF (literal T, TZD required with a time, real calendar day, real time of day, offset within ±14:00), verbatim rather than normalized, else null; raw always keeps the author's bytes and is never emitted; no date is ever derived from the clock, filesystem, filename, or Git history

A reference is the attribute's VALUE — character references resolve before matching, and a URL unify writes into an attribute is escaped for the same reason; then percent-decoded per segment before matching, so the encoded spelling §20.5 publishes resolves exactly as the raw one does; neither is rewritten into the other; per RFC 3986 unreserved escapes decode while a segment decoding to contain / names an impossible file and matches nothing always, including against a file literally named with the escape; a malformed escape leaves its segment as written

--canonical auto (or canonical: auto in unify.yaml) is the whole activation; auto is the only accepted value and any other is a usage error; without it no page changes and nothing is reported; --canonical auto without --base-url is a usage error (exit 2), never a silent no-op or a root-relative canonical

The completed element is <link rel="canonical" href="URL"> with href = record.url HTML-escaped, inserted immediately before </head> reusing that tag's own leading whitespace including its line terminator, everything else byte-identical; a page with no <head> or an unclosed one gets nothing; completion never moves a diagnostic and never changes which pages the sitemap lists

A page declaring any rel=canonical element is left exactly as written — the test is on the DOCUMENT's HEAD, not on the manifest's href value, so an empty or absent href still counts as authored while one in <body> declares nothing and does not suppress completion — including several, one naming another page, and one naming nothing emitted; completion fills a gap and never adjudicates an authored value

Membership is §21.2's predicate unchanged (record, indexable, not 404.html, self-canonical) plus no authored canonical; 404.html because a canonical there is a false claim at every address it is served from, noindex as the conservative default, self-canonical inherited rather than needed

A canonical naming a location the site does not emit is P13 via §12's existing link-href check, authored or completed; multiple canonicals, canonical/noindex, and canonical/sitemap disagreement are audit findings and this section adds no diagnostic for them

Scope is the output-root robots.txt emitted from source; a robots.txt elsewhere in the tree is an ordinary mirror-copied asset (RFC 9309 §2.3 fetches only /robots.txt at the origin); the checks are NOT gated on --base-url, because a root-relative Sitemap: value is internal by inspection and gating it left §12 blocking an identical href while the robots line stayed silent — the flag governs only the stripping step, as in §12; no byte of an authored file is generated, rewritten, or reordered

A Sitemap: value naming a location this site emits must resolve to an emitted file or raise P13 located at the source robots.txt and at the value's own line, with ONE exemption: without --base-url a value naming sitemap.xml or a sitemap-N.xml is skipped, because §21.1 writes those only when the address is known and a flag the author did not set must not fail their correct site; any other missing target still raises P13; internal is §12's own test after --base-url stripping; another origin is skipped rather than fetched; the diagnostic quotes the AUTHORED spelling per §14.1, because §23.1 rewrites no byte of this file and the stripped form appears in none of it — the same holds for an authored sitemap in §21.6; the exemption is silence in the publish path only — audit reports every line it skips as robots-sitemap-missing (AUD-11), from the values this branch hands over rather than from a second read of the file

Disallow/Allow values are patterns and are never checked; a malformed line is inert per RFC 9309 §2.3.1.5 (crawlers use the parseable rules) and the parseable lines around it still are checked; an unknown field is inert per §2.2.4 Other Records, which PERMITS rather than forbids reading non-protocol records and names Sitemap as its example; records split on CR, LF, or CRLF per the RFC's NL; a missing Sitemap: line is never an error even when unify generated a sitemap; page-level noindex versus a listed URL is an audit finding, not a build problem

audit runs the whole pipeline — §5-§13 plus §21 generation and §22 completion when their flags are set — and then evaluates the §20 manifest; it never publishes and prints no --dry-run report, and it evaluates emitted bytes rather than source files so there is no second interpretation of the site

audit writes nothing anywhere: it never creates, cleans, touches, or reads the output directory; --clean and --dry-run describe writing and are usage errors (exit 2) naming the reason, never accepted inertly

a finding is neither a problem nor an advisory: two severities, broken (the output contradicts itself or the standard) and incomplete (absent or inconsistent, possibly chosen), neither of which ever blocks a publish; the distinction is objective and carries no claim about importance

the catalogue is the closed list of 29 finding ids with their exact firing conditions — 24 stated in §24.4 and 5 in §26.3, which is one catalogue split by subject rather than two: title/description missing and duplicate, h1 missing and multiple, title-h1-mismatch, lang-missing, page-orphan, id-duplicate, fragment-missing, jsonld-invalid, schema-incomplete, image-missing-dimensions, metadata-in-body, canonical-noindex, sitemap-noindex, sitemap-canonical-disagree, canonical-scheme-mismatch, text-duplicate, metadata-conflict, robots-sitemap-missing, redirect-loop, jsonld-url-unprefixed, and §26.3's jsonld-headline-mismatch, jsonld-url-mismatch, jsonld-lang-mismatch, jsonld-entity-conflict and date-unusable; every finding but robots-sitemap-missing is a predicate over the §20 manifest, and that one is located at the emitted robots.txt rather than at a page record

the three narrowings: duplicate means IDENTICAL (title and description folded for case and whitespace, text folded for Unicode space separators as §20.3 requires of any consumer that compares it) and never a similarity threshold; title/heading mismatch is containment in either direction and never a distance score; nothing anywhere counts characters, so a short title and a long description are not findings

Both cross-artifact findings read §21.2's classifyCanonical, which answers none/self/elsewhere/unknown, and fire only on elsewhere: never by negating §21.2's membership predicate (a noindex page fails it for an unrelated reason), never on unknown (a mailto:, an empty value, or an absolute canonical with no --base-url to compare against), and never by asking whether a byte-prefix strip happened — another site is a question about the HOST, compared as hosts, so HTTPS://EXAMPLE.COM/x, https://EXAMPLE.com/x, //example.com/x and http://example.com/x are all this page (RFC 3986 §6.2.2.1) while a different host is not; a canonical naming a location the site does not emit stays P13 from §12 rather than becoming a finding, and so does a share image, because §12 has always checked og:/twitter: content — one question, one mechanism, and the stronger one; the scheme that host comparison excludes is AUD-12's finding, not this one

the report is stdout, two lines per finding (path: severity: evidence [id], then a fix line) plus a count line, ordered by source path then finding id; it never contains a score, grade, percentage, ranking, keyword count, or character count in any form; §14 diagnostics still print to stderr

exit codes: 2 invalid usage, 1 a pipeline problem regardless of --strict or findings, 0 findings without --strict, 1 any finding of either severity with --strict; --strict keeps its §14.1 meaning at the same time

metadata-conflict (broken) renders a CLOSED SUBSET of §20.4's conflicts — canonical, title, description, lang, exactly the fields whose own specification says at most one per document — naming the field, the value kept, and the values ignored; image and schemaType are excluded because repeated og:image is how the Open Graph protocol spells an array and a second ld+json entity is recommended practice, author because the HTML spec defines the name as one of the page's authors, robots because §20.6 unions the directives so no conflict remains, and the two dates because article:published_time beside meta name=date names one instant at two granularities; §20.4 and §22.5 both promise this command will report them and product-spec §6.3.2 requires it, so without it a page declaring two canonicals was silent in build AND audit; refresh is recorded in conflicts (§20.4) but is not rendered here, because this list's criterion is a spec-stated at-most-one rule and unify asserts only that the manifest reads the first

Document metadata — title, description, author, robots, datePublished/dateModified, the og:/twitter: metas behind image, and canonical — is read from <head> only; lang, headings, ids, text, linksOut, fragmentLinks, jsonLd, and refresh are deliberately not head-scoped (jsonLd because ld+json is valid and read inside <body>; refresh because §20.11 argues the placement from consequence rather than definition); a document with no <head> element is read whole, because unify's parser does not implement HTML tree construction and cannot place the implied boundary

metadata-in-body (broken) names each document-metadata element emitted outside <head> on a page that HAS one — the closed set is <title>, <base>, <meta charset>, <link rel=canonical>, and metas carrying description/robots/og:*/twitter:*; a page with no head reports nothing, <template> contents are never reported, and elements legal in the body (link rel=stylesheet/preload, meta itemprop, ld+json) are never reported

robots-sitemap-missing (incomplete) reports the residual §23.3's exemption leaves open: without --base-url a Sitemap: value naming sitemap.xml or sitemap-N.xml is skipped by the build check, and audit emits one finding per skipped line, located at the source robots.txt with a null url, in the file's line order, quoting the AUTHORED spelling because §23.1 rewrites no byte of the file; the values are handed over by the branch that skipped them rather than re-read from robots.txt, so the exemption and the finding cannot disagree about which lines they are; incomplete rather than broken because the same audit under --base-url emits the file and reports nothing — the markup is right and only this run's output is absent; a value naming anything else stays P13, a value the site does emit never reaches the exemption, and an absolute value with no address stays skipped

canonical-scheme-mismatch (broken) fires only with --base-url set, when classifyCanonical answers `self` — the canonical resolving, through §12's stripping and §12's resolution, to this page's own OUTPUT PATH, which under a subpath --base-url is weaker than naming the page's address because stripBaseUrl leaves an on-host path that lacks the prefix unchanged — and the canonical's scheme and the base URL's scheme are both http/https and differ — schemes parsed, never matched, so HTTP://EXAMPLE.COM/x and http://example.com:80/x are http (RFC 3986 §3.1) — and it is symmetric, an https canonical under an http --base-url being the same disagreement; it says nothing for a canonical with no scheme of its own (relative, root-relative, which §11.3 absolutizes with the base's own origin, and protocol-relative, which borrows the page's scheme), for a scheme unify cannot compare (ftp:, mailto:, unparseable, or a --base-url that is not http(s)), for classifyCanonical's `elsewhere`/`unknown` (another host or another page, already canonical-noindex/sitemap-canonical-disagree), and with no --base-url at all; classifyCanonical's host comparison still excludes the scheme and §21.2 still has no reason of its own to drop the page, so the three canonical findings partition on one answer and a §22-completed canonical can never fire it; the severity is broken on the page-against-its-own-address contradiction alone, so a noindex page and 404.html fire it too although §21.2 lists neither

The URL part of a <meta http-equiv="refresh"> content is rewritten by all three phases like an href: §11.1 re-roots it against its PROVENANCE file (a layout's url=target.html must not resolve against each consuming page — it silently meant /target.html and /deep/target.html from one line), §11.2 rewrites it to the pretty URL of the page it names, and §11.3 prefixes a root-relative one with the base PATH and never the origin, because a redirect is fetched by the browser already on the page

A <meta http-equiv="refresh"> URL is a reference (P13) in every emitted page: the content grammar is digits (a fractional part skipped), then ; or , then the keyword url in any ASCII case, then =, then the URL, optionally wrapped in matching quotes that are not part of it; a value with no leading digits declares no refresh and a second part not starting with url declares no readable target, so neither is checked; the delay is never part of the test; the diagnostic is located at the URL's own offset inside the attribute value; an element declaring a URL-valued og:/twitter: key as well spells two readings of one content attribute, and the metas' reading keeps it, so no phase rewrites one value twice

A string value inside a parsed <script type="application/ld+json"> is a reference exactly when the property naming it is one of the closed list url, logo, image, thumbnailUrl, contentUrl AND the value is root-relative (one leading slash) and is not a URI template (no { or }) — the criterion is the PROPERTY, never the value's shape, because a shape test blocked the publish of four conforming shapes at once (urlTemplate's RFC 6570 template, an @id, an identifier, a softwareRequirements path); the property carries through arrays and applies at any depth, @id/@type/@context/identifier are excluded by name and the VALUE of a @context key is skipped whole at any depth because a term definition is not data (an inline context defining URL-valued term names, {"@context":{"url":"/vocab#url","image":"/vocab#image"}}, printed two does-not-resolve problems and blocked the publish), the five are a claim about each property and NOT a claim that they are every URL-valued one — mainEntityOfPage, significantLink, relatedLink, acquireLicensePage and a ListItem item are absent and each absence costs a missed check and nothing else, relative and absolute values are not checked (a relative IRI resolves against @base, which this build does not read), keys are never references, a block that does not parse is left to §24.4's jsonld-invalid, a block inside <template> is not read, and the diagnostic is located at the <script> element because a position inside the JSON is not a position in the author's source

refresh is {raw, seconds, url, target} from the FIRST meta http-equiv=refresh whose content declares a refresh (§20.4), null when the page emits none, and read document-wide rather than head-scoped because a redirect §24 cannot see is a redirect nobody checks; target is the record's own output path when the value carries no second part, the resolved output path when it names a page with a record, and null otherwise — including for a second part §12's grammar does not read, which is never folded into "this page"

redirect-loop (broken) fires on every page of a cycle in the refresh graph whose every edge is immediate (seconds 0), self-redirect and a bare content="0" included; a delayed refresh is an ordinary pattern (a kiosk rotation, a page that re-reads itself) and is never reported, an unresolvable or ungrammatical target is never on a chain, and the evidence prints the chain from the page it is reported on

jsonld-url-unprefixed (broken) fires only when --base-url supplies a path prefix other than /, naming each distinct §12 JSON-LD reference — the root-relative value of a URL-valued property, read by §12's own reader — that does not already begin with that prefix, in sorted order — §11 never rewrites a URL inside JSON-LD, so the value resolves in the output tree, passes §12, and names the origin's root rather than the site's at the deploy address; a value already carrying the prefix is right at the address the author named and is not reported

Fragments and duplicate ids are decided by §24.4's findings, never by §12: a link whose path resolves and whose fragment names no id publishes unchanged and blocks nothing, and a duplicated id is reported at the declaring page; the boundary is sharp in both directions — a link whose PATH is broken is still P13 whether or not it carries a fragment, and a link naming an id declared twice draws only that page's id-duplicate, no second finding at the link and no P13, because fragment-missing asks whether the id is present and it is

A host's redirect file is source, never a redirect unify understands: the only redirect it models is an authored meta http-equiv=refresh (§25.1), so _redirects and _routes.json at the source root are A14 when the exclude set holds them back and a byte-for-byte mirror copy when they ship, their contents are never parsed, and a target inside one that names no emitted file is not P13

A reference written in the other Unicode normalization form stays P13: §12 matches byte-exactly after percent-decoding and normalizes neither side, because accepting the link would publish an address only some hosts serve — A16 reports the FILES and §12 keeps reporting the LINK; likewise a host that strips extensions is not a collision, /about.html and /about/ being two addresses that unify emits, with --pretty-urls the site-wide choice whose own collision is P12

Every §26.3 comparison reads the SUBJECT OBJECT of a JSON-LD entry — its data when data is a single object, never an array and never a {"@graph": […]} wrapper — and only that object's own string-valued properties, which is §20.8's bounded reading applied to one more question for the same reason: a graph is several entities and choosing which one is THIS page is a judgement rather than a reading; the cost is that every §26.3 finding is silent on the @graph shape several widely-deployed CMS plugins emit, which is the conservative direction because a claim about the wrong node is worse than no claim

jsonld-headline-mismatch (incomplete) fires when a subject object's @type is Article or BlogPosting and it declares a string headline, the page emits EXACTLY ONE h1, and neither string contains the other after case folding and whitespace collapse; containment in either direction and never a distance score (§8 row 2 prepends, so correct pages nest routinely), exactly one h1 for title-h1-mismatch's reason (none leaves nothing visible to compare, several leaves no answer to which), and incomplete because a headline restating the heading differently is a decision an author may have made

jsonld-url-mismatch (broken) fires when a subject object declares a string url, the page declares a canonical, BOTH resolve through §12's own reader (base stripping, then resolution, then directory URLs to index.html) to an output path this manifest holds, and the two differ; a url on another origin is that site's business and one naming a location the site does not emit is already P13 through §12's closed property list, the stronger answer and the one mechanism

jsonld-lang-mismatch (broken) compares only the PRIMARY SUBTAG, case-insensitively: BCP 47 §2.1.1 makes tags case-insensitive so EN-us and en-US are one tag, and en beside en-GB is a refinement rather than a contradiction, so comparing whole tags or comparing bytes would each accuse a correct page; what is left, en against fr, is one document answering one question twice

jsonld-entity-conflict (broken) fires when two subject objects on one page declare the SAME string @id and DIFFERENT string @type values, one finding per @id in sorted order; the @id is what separates this from the shape §24.4 already blesses, a second ld+json block with a different @type being two entities rather than a contradiction, so this finding never fires on a block that carries no @id

date-unusable (broken) fires when datePublished or dateModified has a non-null raw and a null iso — one finding per field, datePublished first — because such a page declared a date NO consumer can use: not §21.3's lastmod, not §26.6's datePublished, not a crawler, and before this finding every one of them dropped it in silence; the evidence quotes raw, the author's own bytes and the only string they can grep for; product-spec §6.7's malformed half, §20.10's no-derivation rule being the inferred half

A JSON-LD datePublished is deliberately NOT compared with the page's own article:published_time or meta name=date: the two name one instant at two granularities (2026-01-02 beside 2026-01-02T09:30:00Z is no contradiction) and separating the pairs that contradict needs a rule about time zones and about how much of a day a bare date covers, which is the judgement §24.4 already declined for metadata-conflict; a JSON-LD image beside og:image, a JSON-LD description beside the meta, and name beside <title> stay out too, the first two being two legitimate consumers and the third adding a third string to title-h1-mismatch's question

The declaration is <meta name="schema">, produced identically by HTML markup, by Markdown frontmatter schema: (§10.2's ordinary meta synthesis), or by a layout for a whole section — one extraction path (§20.8's schemaType) and one generator; accepted values are exactly WebPage, Article, BlogPosting, CASE-SENSITIVELY, and anything else is P23 located at the declaration (the frontmatter key for a .md page, the element for HTML, at its line when §14.1 can name one); name="schema" is unify's own key defined by no standard, so constraining it constrains unify's vocabulary rather than the author's HTML, and §20.8's schemaType stays general because it also reads an unrestricted JSON-LD @type

A block is generated only when all three hold: schemaType is one of the three accepted values, record.jsonLd is EMPTY (authored JSON-LD always wins — §22.3's rule one artifact over, document-wide rather than head-scoped because ld+json does its job in the body per §24.4's metadata-in-body, and a <template>'s contents are never a declaration), and the emitted document has a closed </head> (§22.2 — no insertion point, and synthesizing one is a structural change this section does not make); there is NO FLAG, the declaration being the whole opt-in, and conditions 1 and 2 together mean the meta is always the surviving source of schemaType

The generated block is one <script type="application/ld+json"> at the end of the emitted <head>, reusing the whitespace before </head> on every line; properties in fixed order, each omitted when its source is absent: @context (https://schema.org), @type, name for WebPage / headline for Article and BlogPosting, description, url (record.canonical else record.url), image (record.image.url), author (A PLAIN STRING), datePublished and dateModified (the iso only, never raw), inLanguage; every value is a RECORD field rather than frontmatter, so an HTML page generates what a Markdown page with the same emitted head generates

author is a plain string and never {"@type":"Person","name":…} because <meta name=author> declares a name and nothing about what kind of thing bears it — asserting Person is the invented claim product-spec §6.1 forbids, and an organization author would be misdescribed by a build that never asked; headline is emitted for Article/BlogPosting and name for WebPage because WebPage defines no headline and Article's headline is the property Google's Article documentation reads; url is the FINAL canonical, which is why §26.7 orders generation after §22

Serialization is fixed so two builds of one tree produce identical bytes: two-space indentation, the table's property order, and every < in the serialized JSON written as \u003c — not decoration, since a description containing </script> would otherwise end the element early and spill the rest of the JSON into the document as text, and \u003c is a JSON string escape so the parsed block is unchanged

Generation runs AFTER §22's completion and BEFORE §20's final manifest, so a page whose canonical --canonical auto supplied generates that URL rather than a second opinion; a build with both features derives the manifest three times and §20.2's deriving-changes-nothing invariant is what makes that safe; §12 then checks the generated block like any other and can only pass (url is the canonical §12 checks as a link href, image is the og:image value §12 checks as a URL-valued meta), which runs anyway for §21.6's reason; --dry-run prints one line beside §22's, and audit runs generation unconditionally because §26 has no flag

The never-generated list is closed: no publisher (an entity the page did not declare), no mainEntityOfPage and no @id (identity, which §12's property list excludes for the same reason), no articleBody/wordCount/keywords from record.text (generated prose and a keyword count, forbidden by name in product-spec §6.1), no isPartOf/breadcrumb/speakable (each needs a structure unify has as links rather than as claims), no image width/height inside the block (they belong to the og:image declaration, whose absence image-missing-dimensions already reports), and no date from any source but an authored well-formed one

Problem: a schema declaration naming a type unify does not generate (§26.4); located at the declaration — the frontmatter key for a .md page, the <meta name="schema"> element for HTML — and CASE-SENSITIVE, because article is not a schema.org type and a declaration that generated nothing in silence is what §14 exists to forbid; the message names the three accepted spellings and the <script type="application/ld+json"> that carries any other vocabulary
